PROVIDER ONBOARDING

Connect sign-in and payments

Generate credentials in each provider’s own dashboard, then enter them under Providers & secrets. Start Razorpay in Test Mode. The portal does not generate third-party credentials.

1. Razorpay Payment Pages (no API keys required)

  1. Open Razorpay Dashboard → Payment Pages → Create Payment Page, in Test Mode first.
  2. Create two pages: Oracle 961 Plan 1 and Oracle 961 Prepaid Plus. Add a Customer Decides Amount price field labeled Amount, with currency USD.
  3. Set minimum and maximum: Plan 1 $300–$10,000; Plan 2 $5,000–$50,000. Add your accurate offering terms, refund policy and contact details.
  4. Publish each page. Open its short link and copy the full https://pages.razorpay.com/… URL into the matching Plan Payment Page URL setting above. Save settings; each configured page activates immediately.
  5. The portal passes ?amount= in whole USD to the Amount field. Verify a test payment at the selected amount. Prefilling is not payment verification; reconcile receipts before activating access.
  6. Set the post-payment return URL to https://www.delta-indices.net/Oracle691. Create separate live pages when ready and replace the URLs. Confirm your account supports USD and the stated offering.

Automatic Payment Page confirmation

  1. On BOTH Razorpay pages, add a required Single Line input field named Portal Reference. Its URL key must be portal_reference. Keep the Amount field and require the same email used for the portal account.
  2. In Razorpay → Account & Settings → Webhooks, add https://www.delta-indices.net/api/razorpay/webhook, choose payment.captured, and choose a strong webhook secret.
  3. Save that identical secret in this portal's Razorpay webhook secret setting. API keys are not required for hosted-page confirmation.
  4. Leave Hosted pages mode false for TEST pages. Test payments create test receipts without live access. After verifying real Razorpay test delivery, replace both URLs with LIVE pages, configure the live webhook, then set Hosted pages mode true.
  5. Matching captured USD payments automatically update My Holdings and the account's subscription access. Invalid signatures are rejected; unmatched payments are flagged in the audit log as payment.review.required. Issuance, transfers and investment rights remain subject to final terms.

Razorpay API checkout (optional alternative)

  1. Sign in to Razorpay Dashboard ↗ and select Test Mode.
  2. Open Account & Settings → API Keys → Generate Key. Save the Key ID and Key Secret; the secret is shown at generation.
  3. In Account & Settings → Webhooks, add a public HTTPS URL ending in /api/razorpay/webhook. Choose a strong webhook secret yourself and select payment.captured. Use the same secret in this portal.
  4. Enter all three values in settings. Turn on checkout after the keys are present. Localhost cannot receive Razorpay webhooks directly; a public HTTPS test endpoint is required.
  5. Confirm USD availability, transaction limits, account activation and business eligibility before switching to Live Mode and replacing the keys.
API keys documentation ↗

2. Google

  1. Open Google Cloud / Google Auth Platform ↗ and create or select a project.
  2. Configure Branding, Audience and the consent screen. Add test users if the application is in testing.
  3. Under Clients, create an OAuth client ID → Web application.
  4. Add the exact callback URL below as an authorized redirect URI. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into this portal’s Google settings.
http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/google/callback

Scopes: openid email profile.

Google OpenID Connect guide ↗

3. Facebook / Meta

  1. Create or select an app at Meta for Developers ↗. Choose the Facebook Login use case applicable to your app.
  2. In the app’s Basic settings, copy the App ID and reveal the App Secret.
  3. Configure Facebook Login’s valid OAuth redirect URI using the callback below. Enable web OAuth login and request email public_profile.
  4. Find the supported Graph API version in the app dashboard or Meta’s version documentation. Enter that exact version in settings, for example v25.0; do not assume the example is your app’s version.
  5. Use app roles/test users while the app is in development. Complete any required review, privacy-policy and data-deletion configuration before public launch. Meta may require an HTTPS callback for your app configuration.
http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/facebook/callback

Facebook Login documentation ↗

4. LinkedIn

  1. Create an app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal ↗, supplying the organization/Page information requested.
  2. Under Products, request Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect.
  3. Under Auth, copy the Client ID and Client Secret and register the exact callback below.
  4. Use openid profile email. If LinkedIn requires HTTPS, use the equivalent HTTPS development or deployment URL and update the portal’s callback setting to match.
http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/linkedin/callback

LinkedIn setup documentation ↗

Before deployment

Use the final HTTPS domain consistently in provider dashboards and callback fields. Ordinary Vercel functions do not retain encrypted local account files; choose a persistent Python backend before deployment. The hardcoded admin/pass fallback accepts loopback access only. Replace the fallback password in My profile before sharing access.
